svg.title: xy from two ridge functions
svg.desc: Four heat maps on the square from −1 to 1, on a sequential colour ramp from dark blue through teal to near white. First, xy, a saddle. Then, after an equals sign, the ridge (x+y)²/4, constant along lines x + y = constant, and after a minus sign the ridge (x−y)²/4, constant along lines x − y = constant; these three share one colour scale from −1 to 1. Last, on its own scale from 0 to 0.20, the error |xy − N(x, y)| of the 22-unit network N(x, y) = S(x+y) − S(x−y), where S is the 10-block midpoint skyline of t²/4 on [−2, 2] with edges −2 + 0.4i and an endpoint unit at t = 2. The largest error on a 41-by-41 grid is 0.20, at the corner (−1, −1).
svg.text: xy as a difference of two ridges
colour scale for the three function panels
each ridge is constant along one family of diagonals
xy = ¼(x+y)² − ¼(x−y)²: two skylines of 11 units each give a one-hidden-layer network.
